memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make the ephod of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen — the work of skilled hands. It is to have two shoulder pieces attached to two of its corners, so it can be fastened. Its skillfully woven waistband is to be like it — of one piece with the ephod and made with gold, and with blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and with finely twisted linen." - Exodus 28:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ephod was the central garment, a kind of apron worn over the robe, woven from gold thread and coloured yarn by skilled hands. Its waistband was made of one piece with the ephod itself — not attached afterwards, but woven together from the start, so that the whole garment held as one.

God repeatedly emphasises this "one piece" construction throughout the tabernacle instructions. The lampstand, the cherubim on the mercy seat, and now the ephod. He seems to care that things be integrated rather than assembled — whole rather than patched together.

There is something here for our own lives. We tend to compartmentalise: a work self, a church self, a family self, a private self, each woven separately and stitched loosely together. But God is after wholeness. He wants the faith you profess on Sunday woven into the person you are on Tuesday. James warns against being double-minded and unstable in all our ways (Jas 1:8). Ask God to make you one piece — the same person in every room, integrated rather than fragmented, with your faith running through the whole cloth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I the same person in every part of my life, or divided into separate selves?
Where does my faith need to be woven more deeply into my daily reality?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me whole rather than fragmented. Weave my faith through every part of my life so that I am the same person in every room, integrated and true. Amen.
